chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Amr ibn Uthman and from his father, all together, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: While Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was in the gathering of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), a group of people came and said, 'O Abu Muhammad, we seek Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him).' He said, 'What is your need?' They said, 'We want to ask him a question.' He said, 'And what is it? Inform us of it.' They said, 'A woman, her husband copulated with her. When he rose from her, she rose with her warmth, and fell upon a virgin slave-girl, and pressed against her, so the sperm fell into her, and she became pregnant. What do you say about this?'

Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'It is a dilemma, and Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) is suited for it. And I say: If I am correct, it is from Allah, then from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him); and if I err, it is from myself. So I hope that I will not err, God willing. One should proceed against the woman and take from her the dowry of the virgin slave-girl during the first opportunity, because the child will not exit from her until she is split, so her virginity will be lost. Then the woman will be stoned because she is married (muhsan). Then the slave-girl will be awaited until she gives birth to what is in her belly, and the child will be returned to its father, the owner of the sperm. Then the slave-girl will be whipped with the Hadd.'

He (Muhammad ibn Muslim) said: So the people departed from the presence of Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and met Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him). They said, 'What did you say to Abu Muhammad and what did he say to you?' So they informed him. He said, 'Had I been the one questioned, I would not have had more knowledge about it than what my son said.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for pregnancy resulting from a married woman's intercourse with a virgin slave-girl?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the high level of juristic precision (fiqh) possessed by the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically highlighting the confidence of Imam Ali (AS) in his son Imam Hasan (AS), as he acknowledges that his own knowledge would not exceed Hasan's in this complex case. The ruling details the specific legal consequences for a married woman (rajm) and a virgin slave-girl (hadd) involved in sexual acts with each other, while clarifying the lineage of the resulting child. It serves as a key example of how the Imams derived intricate legal rulings from the Quran and Sunnah, demonstrating their role as the primary interpreters of divine law.
